\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ماجرا} (mâjarâ)}{ماجرا (mâjarâ)}]{\fa{ماجرا} (mâjarâ) — what happened, an affair; an adventure}

\label{lesson:FA-C346-majara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a storyteller, then the Persian for a narrator.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ماجرا}}
\textbf{\fa{ماجرا}} (\emph{mâjarâ}) — \textquotedblleft{}what happened, an affair; an adventure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{همه} \fa{ماجرا} \fa{را} \fa{برای} \fa{پلیس} \fa{گفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U hame-ye mâjarâ râ barâ-ye polis goft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He told the police the whole story of what happened.
\end{quote}

\emph{Mâjarâ chi bud?} \textquotedblleft{}What was it all about?\textquotedblright{} \emph{Mâjarâju} is \textquotedblleft{}an adventurer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mâjarâ} is usually explained as the Arabic phrase \emph{mā jarā}, \textquotedblleft{}what took place\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists the Persian word without a parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mâjarâ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mâjarâ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{mâjarâ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a storyteller, then the Persian for a narrator, then say \emph{mâjarâ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{روایت} (revâyat)}{روایت (revâyat)}]{\fa{روایت} (revâyat) — an account, a narrative}

\label{lesson:FA-C346-revayat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a narrator, then the Persian for what happened.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{روایت}}
\textbf{\fa{روایت}} (\emph{revâyat}) — \textquotedblleft{}an account, a narrative\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{روایت} \fa{او} \fa{با} \fa{روایت} \fa{پلیس} \fa{فرق} \fa{داشت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Revâyat-e u bâ revâyat-e polis farq dâsht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
His account differed from the police account.
\end{quote}

\emph{Be revâyat-e ...} \textquotedblleft{}according to ...\textquotedblright{}. Also a traditional report of a saying.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{revâyat} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{riwāya}, \textquotedblleft{}narration, transmission\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{revâyat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{revâyat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{revâyat}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a narrator, then the Persian for what happened, then say \emph{revâyat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{روایت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An account, a narrative\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{روایت} \fa{کردن} (revâyat kardan)}{روایت کردن (revâyat kardan)}]{\fa{روایت} \fa{کردن} (revâyat kardan) — to narrate, to recount}

\label{lesson:FA-C346-revayat-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for what happened, then the Persian for an account.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{روایت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{روایت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{revâyat kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to narrate, to recount\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{فیلم} \fa{داستان} \fa{یک} \fa{خانواده} \fa{را} \fa{روایت} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Film dâstân-e yek khânevâde râ revâyat mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The film tells the story of a family.
\end{quote}

Present \emph{revâyat mikonad}. More literary than \emph{ta'rif kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{revâyat kardan} joins \emph{revâyat} \textquotedblleft{}an account\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{riwāya}, with \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{revâyat kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{revâyat kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{revâyat kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for what happened, then the Persian for an account, then say \emph{revâyat kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{روایت} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To narrate, to recount\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نقل} \fa{کردن} (naql kardan)}{نقل کردن (naql kardan)}]{\fa{نقل} \fa{کردن} (naql kardan) — to relate, to pass on (a story)}

\label{lesson:FA-C346-naql-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an account, then the Persian for to narrate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نقل} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{نقل} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{naql kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to relate, to pass on (a story)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدرم} \fa{این} \fa{خاطره} \fa{را} \fa{بارها} \fa{نقل} \fa{کرده} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pedaram in khâtere râ bâr-hâ naql karde ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father has told this memory many times.
\end{quote}

Also \textquotedblleft{}to quote\textquotedblright{}: \emph{az u naql kard} \textquotedblleft{}he quoted him\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{naql mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{naql} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{naql}, \textquotedblleft{}transport, transfer\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): a story carried from one teller to the next. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naql kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naql kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{naql kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an account, then the Persian for to narrate, then say \emph{naql kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{یادآوری} \fa{کردن} (yâdâvari kardan)}{یادآوری کردن (yâdâvari kardan)}]{\fa{یادآوری} \fa{کردن} (yâdâvari kardan) — to remind}

\label{lesson:FA-C346-yadavari-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to narrate, then the Persian for to relate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{یادآوری} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{یادآوری} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{yâdâvari kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to remind\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{منشی} \fa{جلسه} \fa{فردا} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{ما} \fa{یادآوری} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Monshi jalase-ye fardâ râ be mâ yâdâvari kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The secretary reminded us about tomorrow's meeting.
\end{quote}

The thing takes \emph{râ}, the person \emph{be}. \emph{yâd} \textquotedblleft{}memory\textquotedblright{} + \emph{âvari} \textquotedblleft{}bringing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{yâdâvari} joins \emph{yâd} \textquotedblleft{}memory\textquotedblright{} and \emph{âvari} \textquotedblleft{}bringing\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{âvardan} \textquotedblleft{}to bring\textquotedblright{}: bringing to mind. All of it is native Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}
